value.rationale: The threshold z/n is the natural Haar scale with cap probability tending to e^{-z}, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The strict full-Laplace-clock comparison quantifies the counterintuitive effect of growing state-space dimension while maintaining fixed equilibrium rarity. The exact positive finite-size delay is a usable benchmark, and the Bessel-to-exponential complete law differentiates typical and rare state-search times beyond previously published mean and long-time-tail formulas. These constitute one coherent physically motivated characterization, not a routine numerical recomputation.
